request:
Our campus has a lost-and-found desk and we want a simple board for it. Anyone who finds something can report it with a short description of the item, where they found it and the date they found it. People should be able to see all the items on the board and look at one item. When the owner comes to collect an item, the desk marks it as claimed and writes down the owner's name. An item that has already been claimed cannot be claimed again. We also want to see only the items that are still waiting for their owners.

The client's answers to your questions:
Q: Should the owner's name be the only thing recorded when an item is claimed, or do you also want something like the date claimed or a way to check the owner's ID?
A: No preference: you decide.
Q: Who can do what? Can anyone report and view items, and only desk staff mark items as claimed, and if so how should the desk sign in?
A: No preference: you decide.
Q: Should reports include a photo or contact details of the finder, and should claimed items stay on the board or be removed after a while?
A: No, they stay on the full list, but the list of waiting items should only show unclaimed ones.

Where the client has no preference or did not answer, choose the simplest option and add nothing they did not ask for (no logins, PINs or extra required fields).
summary:
I wrote `app.py` and `tests/test_app.py`, and both tests pass. I didn't start the server or try it by hand. Items are stored in a SQLite file, `lostfound.db`, in the project folder.

- `POST /items` reports a found item. It needs `description`, `location` and `date_found` (YYYY-MM-DD). It returns 201 with the new item. Missing or blank fields and bad dates get a 422.
- `GET /items` lists every item, claimed ones included.
- `GET /items/unclaimed` lists only the items still waiting for their owners.
- `GET /items/{id}` shows one item, or a 404 if it doesn't exist.
- `POST /items/{id}/claim` marks the item as claimed. It takes `{"owner_name": "..."}` and returns the updated item. A blank or missing name gets a 422, an unknown item gets a 404, and an item that is already claimed gets a 409.

An item shows `claimed` (true or false) and `owner_name`. There are no logins, so anyone can report, view or claim an item. I recorded only the owner's name, with no claim date or ID check.
